requirements.requirement: The system must call the EVAL-COMPARE API with a list of selected provider IDs when the comparison view is initialized.
The system must update application state with the API response and pass normalized comparison data to the comparison UI component.
The system must display a loading state indicator while the EVAL-COMPARE API request is in progress.
The system must render the comparison UI component only after a successful API response is received and mapped.
The system must allow users to dynamically add a provider to the comparison and trigger a new API request reflecting the updated provider set.
The system must allow users to remove a provider from the comparison and update the UI and state accordingly without requiring a full page reload.
The system must handle API errors by displaying a user-visible error state with a retry option.
The system must handle empty or malformed API responses by preventing UI rendering and showing a fallback error message.
The system must maintain synchronization between selected providers in state and the providers displayed in the comparison UI.
The system must reuse API integration patterns consistent with App.tsx for request handling, state updates, and side effects.
The system must ensure that repeated identical provider selections do not trigger redundant API calls.
The system must preserve previously loaded comparison data in state while a new API request is pending for updated provider selections.
The system must log API request failures and response anomalies for debugging and monitoring purposes.
The system must ensure that LLM-generated comparison summaries (if present in API response) are rendered without modification to their semantic meaning.
The system must ensure that LLM-generated fields are clearly associated with their corresponding providers and measures in the UI.
The system must not fabricate or infer missing comparison data when the API response lacks specific measures or scores.
The system must display partial comparison results if at least one provider's data is successfully returned while others fail.
The system must ensure that concurrent API requests resolve in order and do not overwrite newer state with stale responses.
